disease.disease_type.sql_expression: TRIM(CASE WHEN INSTR(disease_type, '||') > 0 THEN SUBSTR(disease_type, 1, INSTR(disease_type, '||') - 1) ELSE disease_type END)
disease.disease_type.reason: The query treats disease_type as one category per row, grouping by it and excluding ''. The stored values are multi-category lists such as 'infectious||inflammatory', so grouping by the raw string creates a separate group for each combination. Keeping only the first listed category gives one category per disease, and the expression works deterministically on every stored value, including single-item ones. This drops secondary categories, and a map cannot return several categories per row, so this is the closest fit to the author's intent.

If the primary indication has no counterpart in the partner list, map it to the closest partner disease it clearly corresponds to, or to NULL so the inner join drops it. Each drug ends up with exactly one disease name.
